summary: Investigation into newgame.dbs record structure via consumer-trace approach (tracing wpcmk.ovr reads). KEY FINDING: wpcmk does NOT read newgame.dbs at all. The consumer-trace approach failed because the assumed consumer (wpcmk) is not a consumer of this file. Race stat floor data lives in wroot DGROUP BSS, populated at runtime by a different pathway (winit). Direct byte-pattern searches in newgame.dbs also yielded no useful results.

findings.claim: wpcmk.ovr does not access newgame.dbs at all. The consumer-trace approach produced a null result.

evidence.all_strings_found: NONE of the above found in wpcmk.ovr (24793 bytes)
evidence.method: python data.find() on binary content; also data.count(b'\xcd\x21') == 0

findings.claim: Race base stat floor tables are in wroot DGROUP BSS at addresses 0x52d9..0x5333 (11 races × 9 bytes stride). These are ZERO at file load time and populated at runtime — almost certainly by winit.ovr state-0 which loads MASTER.HDR and/or DISK.HDR and scenario databases.
findings.implication: To decode newgame.dbs race record offsets, we need to trace winit.ovr state-0 to find where race data is loaded and at what DGROUP address. The DGROUP load base for the race table would let us compute: newgame_offset = dgroup_load_base - 0x52d9 (inverted).

findings.claim: Direct pattern searches in newgame.dbs for race stat data produced no useful matches.

searches_attempted.pattern: A-encoded race stat tables (8 bytes, values like 0x48 'H'=7, 0x4b 'K'=10, etc.)
searches_attempted.method: Searched for known Elf pattern HKNJJJIE (NOBAL attrs minus racial floors) — 0 matches

searches_attempted.result: 296 false-positive matches (sequential counter data around offset 0xc16)

findings.claim: newgame.dbs is 49856 bytes (0xc2c0). Structure not decoded. Content not identifiable from wpcmk consumer trace or direct pattern matching.

evidence.status: UNKNOWN — requires winit.ovr state-0 trace or dynamic DOSBox-X memory snapshot

unresolved: newgame.dbs record structure: unknown. Needs winit.ovr state-0 ASM trace to find where the file is opened and parsed, then decode what data is extracted and stored to DGROUP.
Which specific file (newgame.dbs, MASTER.HDR, DISK.HDR, scenario.dbs) contains race stat floor data — unknown. winit state-0 loads multiple database files.

Dynamic approach alternative: use DOSBox-X save-state MCP tools to snapshot DGROUP memory after winit state-0 completes (game_state transitions from 0 to 1), read DGROUP 0x52d9..0x5333 to get the actual race stat floor values without needing to trace the file I/O.
recommended_next_step: Use dosbox_read_memory MCP tool on a save state captured after winit state-0 (game is past loading screen, in main menu). Read DGROUP offset 0x52d9, length 0x5a (90 bytes = 11 races × 9 bytes). This gives the actual runtime race stat floor values directly, bypassing the need to decode newgame.dbs format.
